findings.title: Font-size refit emits session:resize with no visibility guard
findings.why_it_matters: The new font-size effect calls `fitAddonRef.current?.fit()` and then `socket.emit('session:resize', ...)` unconditionally, whenever the app-wide `codeFontSize` setting changes. Every other call site in this same file that does fit()+emit (lines 229-235, 243-248, 261, 368-372) first checks `container.offsetWidth > 0 && container.offsetHeight > 0` before touching the pty size — this new one is the only one that doesn't. Focus.tsx keeps the terminal mounted with its container collapsed to `flex: 0 0 0px` while a Diff/Explorer workbench is maximized (comment at Focus.tsx:251-253: 'The terminal stays mounted at all times... it collapses to 0 height'). `@xterm/addon-fit`'s `proposeDimensions()` clamps degenerate sizes to `Math.max(2, ...)` cols / `Math.max(1, ...)` rows instead of bailing out (only NaN short-circuits), so fitting a 0-height container silently succeeds and returns `{cols:2, rows:1}`. The subsequent emit sends that to the server, whose `session:resize` handler resizes the real tmux pane to whichever client reports the largest dims (server/src/socket/handler.ts:44-61) — if the maximized Focus tile is the only viewer of that session, the pty is genuinely resized to 2x1, garbling live output for every future viewer until something else triggers a correct refit. Changing the font size while a workbench panel is maximized (a completely ordinary sequence: open Explorer, then bump font size in settings) reproduces this every time.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the fit()+emit pair the same way every other call site in this file does: `const c = containerRef.current; if (c && c.offsetWidth > 0 && c.offsetHeight > 0) { fitAddonRef.current?.fit(); socket.emit('session:resize', { sessionId, cols: t.cols, rows: t.rows }); }`. Keep `t.options.fontSize = codeFontSize;` unconditional (it's a local style-only op). When the tile becomes visible again, the existing `terminal:refit` dispatch in Focus.tsx's `restoreToShell` (and the ResizeObserver/visibilitychange handlers) will fit+emit correct dimensions at the new font size.
evidence: client/src/hooks/useTerminal.ts:437-445: `useEffect(() => { const t = terminalRef.current; if (!t || t.options.fontSize === codeFontSize) return; t.options.fontSize = codeFontSize; fitAddonRef.current?.fit(); socket.emit('session:resize', { sessionId, cols: t.cols, rows: t.rows }); }, [codeFontSize, sessionId, socket]);` — no container-size check, unlike lines 228-236 and 355-378 in the same file.

client/src/app/views/Focus.tsx:251-253/255: comment 'The terminal stays mounted at all times; when a tool window is maximized it collapses to 0 height' and `style={{ flex: maximized ? '0 0 0px' : 1, ... }}` on the div wrapping `<TerminalShell>`.

node_modules/@xterm/addon-fit/lib/addon-fit.js: `proposeDimensions()` returns `{cols: Math.max(2, floor(...)), rows: Math.max(1, floor(...))}` for a zero-height container instead of returning undefined, so `fit()` proceeds and resizes the terminal to 2x1.

server/src/socket/handler.ts:137-148: `session:resize` stores the reporting client's dims and resizes the pty via `getSessionDimensions` (largest desktop client, or smallest mobile client if any) — a lone 2x1 report from the only connected viewer becomes the pty's real size.

residual_risks: The font-size refit effect (useTerminal.ts:437-445) has no debounce, unlike the ResizeObserver-driven doFit() (100ms) and terminal:refit handler (50ms) in the same hook. A font-size control that emits many intermediate values in quick succession (e.g. a live-dragged slider rather than discrete +/- steps) will fire fit()+session:resize once per intermediate value with no coalescing — likely just wasted socket traffic today, but worth confirming the actual font-size UI only emits on commit, not on every drag tick.

authFetch's new `intercept401` opt-out is currently only exercised by `login()`; if a future protected endpoint needs the same treatment (e.g. a 401 that carries a domain-specific error rather than session expiry) it's easy to forget the opt-out and get an unwanted forced logout — worth a code comment pointer at the `authFetch` definition site (already present) but no test currently pins the *default* (intercept401 undefined/true) path against a genuinely protected route beyond auth/status and ngrok/status, both of which are on the server's public-path allowlist and can never actually 401.
testing_gaps: No test exercises useTerminal's font-size effect against a zero-size (hidden/collapsed) container to confirm session:resize isn't emitted with degenerate dimensions — the Focus.tsx maximized-workbench scenario that triggers this isn't covered by any client test.

api.test.ts's new suite covers authFetch's intercept401 behavior for login() in isolation, but doesn't test two concurrent authFetch calls racing on the same 401 (both clearing/dispatching) to confirm no double-navigation or lost-request state in ArgusApp/MobileApp's `auth:unauthorized` handlers.
